title: Although: aunque and the limits of change

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *aunque* ("although") from A2 Unit 28. It joins two facts that seem to pull in different directions. In this lesson it shows how society changed even when rights stayed limited: *Aunque las mujeres no podían votar, muchas trabajaban*.

items.spanish: Aunque las mujeres no podían votar, muchas trabajaban como maestras.
items.english: Although women could not vote, many worked as teachers.

items.spanish: Aunque la universidad era pública, tenía demasiado control de la Iglesia.
items.english: Although the university was public, it had too much control by the Church.

items.spanish: Aunque el poder seguía en manos de grupos pequeños, muchos pedían más derechos.
items.english: Although power stayed in the hands of small groups, many were asking for more rights.

items.spanish: Muchas mujeres trabajaban fuera de casa, aunque tenían menos derechos que los hombres.
items.english: Many women worked outside the home, although they had fewer rights than men.

sections.content: With facts, the verb after *aunque* is in the indicative (*no podían*, *era*). The clause with *aunque* can come first or second; put a comma after it when it comes first.
